rv.q: We Had a World is a thoughtful if sedate staging of duty, care and the relational ties that can't be shaken loose.
A World is beautifully written, wonderfully acted and sensitively directed.
Director Josh Seymour marshals terrific performances from this superb trio.
The end result, I am happy to report, is a delicious and spicy ensemble piece worthy of Edward Albee.
The narratorial meta-theatrics often irk, and the conflict can be repetitive, but Harmon delivers plenty of laughs and gets squabbling families spot-on.
The psychological meat of the relationships between the three characters is sturdy enough to stand on its own.
